title: Practice Exam 4
description: A fourth full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: When the road is wet and you begin to hydroplane, you should:
choices: Ease off the gas and avoid sudden braking or steering
Brake hard immediately
Accelerate to regain traction
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), gently ease off the accelerator and keep the wheel steady. Avoid hard braking or sharp steering until traction returns. Slowing down in the rain prevents it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving in the Rain

questions.question: Driving 'too fast for conditions' on an icy road, even at the posted limit, is:
choices: A violation of the basic speed law
Always legal at the posted speed
Only a problem at night
questions.explanation: The basic speed law requires you to drive at a safe speed for current conditions. On ice or in heavy rain, the safe speed may be far below the posted limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Basic Speed Law

questions.question: A sign reading 'SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT' means:
choices: If you are going slower than other traffic, move to the right lane
All traffic must use the right lane
Slow down and stay where you are
questions.explanation: This sign tells slower drivers to use the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left, improving flow and safety.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Signs

questions.question: A 'WRONG WAY' sign means:
choices: You are traveling against traffic and must turn around safely
The road ahead is closed
Make a U-turn immediately, anywhere
questions.explanation: A red 'WRONG WAY' sign warns that you are going the wrong direction, often on a one-way street or freeway ramp. Slow down, pull over, and safely turn around.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Regulatory Signs

questions.question: When two vehicles meet on a narrow mountain road where neither can pass, who has the right of way?
choices: The vehicle heading uphill
The vehicle heading downhill
The larger vehicle
questions.explanation: On a steep, narrow mountain road, the vehicle going downhill must yield by backing up if needed, because the uphill vehicle has more control backing up the grade.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Mountain Driving

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a stop sign on your road but cross traffic does not stop, you must:
choices: Stop and yield to the cross traffic before proceeding
Proceed because you stopped first
Expect cross traffic to stop for you
questions.explanation: A stop sign on your side only stops your traffic. You must yield to cross traffic that does not have a stop sign before entering the intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stop Signs

questions.question: On a one-way street, you may change lanes:
choices: Freely when clear, since all traffic moves the same direction
Never
Only by stopping first
questions.explanation: On a one-way street all lanes move the same way, so you may change lanes when it is clear. Still signal and check your blind spots.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — One-Way Streets

questions.question: Weaving in and out of traffic to gain a few car lengths:
choices: Increases crash risk and rarely saves time
Is the safest way to travel
Is encouraged in heavy traffic
questions.explanation: Frequent, aggressive lane changes greatly increase collision risk and rarely get you there faster. Pick a lane and maintain a steady, safe speed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Safe Lane Use

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
choices: Greater than the normal three seconds
Less than normal
Exactly one second
questions.explanation: On wet, icy, or gravel surfaces, traction is reduced and stopping takes longer, so increase your following distance well beyond three seconds.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance in Poor Conditions

questions.question: A 'space cushion' around your vehicle helps you:
choices: Have room to react and avoid hazards
Drive faster legally
Park more easily
questions.explanation: Keeping space ahead, behind, and to the sides gives you time and room to see hazards and maneuver safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Managing Space

questions.question: If you refuse to take a chemical test after a lawful DUI arrest, you will:
choices: Face an automatic license suspension
Avoid all penalties
Receive only a warning
questions.explanation: Under the implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a lawful DUI arrest results in an automatic license suspension and additional penalties.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Refusing a Chemical Test

questions.question: The legal BAC limit for drivers operating a commercial vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers may not operate with a BAC of 0.04% or higher — half the limit for regular drivers.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Commercial Driver BAC

questions.question: When you see a 'School Zone — 25 mph When Children Are Present' sign, you should:
choices: Slow to 25 mph or less whenever children are nearby
Maintain the regular street speed
Slow down only on school days at noon
questions.explanation: Where signs post a reduced school-zone speed when children are present, you must slow to that limit (often 25 mph or less) whenever children are in the area.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Zone Speed Limits

questions.question: When children are playing near the street or you see a ball roll into the road, you should:
choices: Slow down and be ready to stop, as a child may follow
Maintain speed and honk
Swerve into the other lane
questions.explanation: A ball or toy in the road often means a child may run after it. Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Watching for Children

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signal is green, you should:
choices: Obey the officer, even if it contradicts the signal
Follow the green light instead
Stop and wait for the signal to change
questions.explanation: Directions from a police officer or authorized person always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Obeying Officers

questions.question: You may not drive over a fire hose at the scene of a fire unless:
choices: A fire official directs you to do so
You are in a hurry
No firefighters are visible
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive over an unprotected fire hose without permission from a fire department official.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Fire Scenes

questions.question: When passing a pedestrian walking along a road with no sidewalk, you should:
choices: Slow down and give them as much room as possible
Maintain speed and stay in your lane
Honk continuously
questions.explanation: Give pedestrians walking on the roadway extra space and reduce speed, especially where there is no sidewalk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Pedestrians

questions.question: Before opening your car door on the traffic side after parking, you should:
choices: Check for approaching cars and bicyclists
Open it quickly to get out
Rely on other drivers to avoid you
questions.explanation: Always check mirrors and look back for cars and bicyclists before opening a door into traffic. 'Dooring' a cyclist can cause serious injury and is illegal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Opening Doors Safely

questions.question: A yellow painted curb means:
choices: Stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight
No stopping at any time
Free unlimited parking
questions.explanation: A yellow curb is a loading zone — stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, within the posted time limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: Parking in a space marked for persons with disabilities without a valid placard or plate:
choices: Is illegal and can result in a heavy fine
Is allowed for short stops
Is fine if no disabled driver is present
questions.explanation: Only vehicles displaying a valid disabled-person placard or plate may use these spaces. Violations carry significant fines.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Disabled Parking

questions.question: When traffic is merging onto the freeway and you are in the right lane, the courteous and safe action is to:
choices: Move over a lane if it is safe, or adjust speed to allow merging
Speed up to block the merge
Stop in your lane
questions.explanation: Help merging traffic by moving over when safe or adjusting your speed to open a gap. Cooperative merging keeps traffic flowing safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Freeway Merging

questions.question: Highway hypnosis or drowsiness on a long freeway drive is best handled by:
choices: Stopping to rest, getting fresh air, or switching drivers
Driving faster to finish sooner
Turning the heater up
questions.explanation: Fatigue seriously impairs driving. Stop and rest, take a break, get fresh air, or change drivers. Never rely on tricks to stay awake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Fatigue and Driving

questions.question: Setting up your GPS or playlist is safest when done:
choices: Before you start driving, while parked
While driving slowly
At every red light
questions.explanation: Program your GPS and choose your music before you begin driving. Adjusting devices while moving takes your eyes and mind off the road.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Avoiding Distractions

questions.question: Which is the most accurate statement about multitasking while driving?
choices: The brain cannot fully focus on driving and another task at once
Experienced drivers can safely text
Hands-free means distraction-free
questions.explanation: Research shows the brain switches between tasks rather than truly multitasking. Even hands-free phone use causes 'inattention blindness,' so driving deserves your full attention.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cognitive Distraction

questions.question: A green traffic light means:
choices: Proceed if the intersection is clear
Speed up before it turns yellow
Stop and check for cross traffic
questions.explanation: A green light means you may go if the way is clear. You must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians lawfully in the intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: If you are approaching a yellow light and you are too close to stop safely, you should:
choices: Continue through the intersection with caution
Slam on the brakes
Speed up well above the limit
questions.explanation: If you cannot stop safely when the light turns yellow, proceed through with caution. Hard braking risks a rear-end collision.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Yellow Light

questions.question: A lane signal showing a steady downward green arrow means:
choices: You may use this lane
The lane is closed ahead
Move out of the lane immediately
questions.explanation: A steady downward green arrow over a lane means it is open for you to drive in. A red X means the lane is closed and you must move out of it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Signals

questions.question: At an intersection with a green light, a pedestrian steps off the curb against the signal. You should:
choices: Yield to the pedestrian to avoid a collision
Proceed because you have the green
Honk and continue at speed
questions.explanation: Even when a pedestrian is crossing illegally, you must do everything reasonable to avoid hitting them. Safety comes before right of way.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrian Safety

questions.question: Diagonal yellow-and-black striped markings on the pavement indicate:
choices: An obstruction or median you must not drive over
A parking area
A passing zone
questions.explanation: Yellow-and-black diagonal stripes mark a fixed obstruction or median. Keep to the marked travel lane and do not drive across them.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pavement Markings

questions.question: When parking downhill without a curb, turn your wheels:
choices: Toward the edge of the road
Away from the edge of the road
Straight ahead
questions.explanation: Downhill with no curb, point your wheels toward the edge of the road so a rolling car would leave the roadway rather than enter traffic. Set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: The speed limit in an alley is:
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
10 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in any alley is 15 mph. Watch carefully for pedestrians and vehicles entering or exiting.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: When approaching a curve, you should:
choices: Slow down before entering the curve
Brake hard in the middle of the curve
Accelerate hard into the curve
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before you enter a curve. Braking in the curve can cause a skid; slow down first, then accelerate gently out of it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Through Curves

questions.question: Open containers of alcohol in the passenger area of a vehicle are:
choices: Illegal, even if the driver has not been drinking
Legal if the bottle is half full
Allowed for passengers only
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have an open container of alcohol in the passenger compartment, whether or not anyone is drinking from it. Store it in the trunk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Open Container Law

questions.question: When you see a bicyclist signaling a left turn, you should:
choices: Yield and allow the cyclist to move left as a vehicle would
Pass on the left quickly
Ignore the signal
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may use the traffic lane to turn left, just like a car. Yield to a signaling cyclist and give them room to complete the turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicyclists Turning

questions.question: When driving on the freeway, you should keep your eyes moving and scan:
choices: Far ahead as well as your mirrors and sides
Only the car directly in front of you
Only the speedometer
questions.explanation: Good drivers scan far ahead (10–15 seconds), check mirrors regularly, and stay aware of vehicles beside them to anticipate hazards early.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Scanning the Road

questions.question: You want to change lanes but a car is in your blind spot. You should:
choices: Wait until the lane is clear before moving over
Change lanes anyway and let them brake
Speed up and cut in front
questions.explanation: Never change lanes when a vehicle is in your blind spot. Adjust your speed and wait until you can clearly see the lane is open.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Blind Spots
